requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.
rationale:
**Confirmation:** the assessments disagreed

First assessment `true`: structural: `requirements.cli.bootstrap_skill` prescribes no library, algorithm, signature, type, field or named interface. Each clause is a content or behavior obligation:
- "Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase". Any packaging that ships the skill satisfies it. `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md` exists, and `Cargo.toml` points the skills source path at `assets/skills`. No particular mechanism is mandated.
- "direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test... map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality... report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review". These describe what the skill's text says. A differently worded or organized skill with the same directions would satisfy them, so the wording is discretionary.

The root `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md` also supports each of those directions. The `Inventories` section covers all of the following:
- A Tests inventory of "every first-party runnable test or test case".
- An Items and behavior inventory covering every Rust function, method, struct, enum and union, plus the observable surface.
- A Gap list.
- An exclusion rule for third-party and generated code.

The `Report` section requires "Tests mapped", "Items mapped" and "Independent recount" lines, plus a list of gaps. It says to claim 100% only when both inventories have no unmapped items, the recount agrees, and every observable branch has been reviewed.

No structural obligation is left without implementation evidence.

behavioral: The one marked test, `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bootstrap_skill_is_bundled_and_directs_complete_inventories]`, covers each obligation in `requirements.cli.bootstrap_skill`. The helpers `assert_phrases` and `assert_in_order` check the bundled skill text through `assert_text` and `assert_text_in_order`. Those two helpers assert that each phrase is present and, for the ordered one, that each phrase comes after the previous one. I read `assert_phrases` and the excerpts of the other helpers, not their full bodies.

- **Bundled skill:** the test asserts `SKILLS` contains `habeas-bootstrap-requirements`. It also asserts the front-matter description starts with "Use when adopting Habeas in an existing codebase". The phrase checks read the skill from the bundled files.
- **Read the code and tests:** the test asserts the phrases "Read the existing requirements, documentation, public entry points, implementation, and tests" and "Follow behavior through the code".
- **Map every first-party test to a requirement or example:** the test asserts "every first-party runnable test or test case", "Record the behavior each test checks; fill in requirement names…", and "Every test must end up with a `{test}` reference to a requirement or example".
- **Identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality:** the test asserts the source-unit inventory phrase ("every function, method, struct, enum, and union, listed from the source…"). It also asserts the end-user-visible categories phrase ("public APIs, commands, handlers, UI actions, configuration, outputs, errors, and distinct observable branches"), the warning that a tagged entry point doesn't cover every branch beneath it, and "Give every inventoried test and each requirement's roots their references".
- **Report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review:** the test asserts, in order, the independent recount phrase ("recount both inventories from the source and tests without your lists"). It then asserts the gap-report line format, "Claim 100% only when both inventories have no unmapped items", and "Don't silently exclude difficult cases".

A skill that dropped any of these directives would fail the test. I found no unchecked behavioral obligation and no marking gap.

Second assessment `false`: In `tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bootstrap_skill_is_bundled_and_directs_complete_inventories]`, extend the ordered assertions so the completeness-claim gate is checked in full. Assert the rest of the sentence after "Claim 100% only when both inventories have no unmapped items", namely ", the independent recount agrees, and every observable branch has been reviewed". Also assert the Report line "Independent recount: <agrees | differences and how reconciled>". Optionally assert "Map each other inventoried item to the requirement whose root reaches it" and "goes on the gap list", so that mapping source units to requirements is checked beyond the inventory and root-tagging phrases. — The requirement says the skill MUST direct agents to "report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review". The test does check that the skill is bundled, since `SKILLS` lists it, `description` starts as expected, and the `SKILL.md` text comes from `include_str!`. It also checks the read-code-and-tests phrases, the test-inventory phrases, the source-unit inventory phrases, the `Gaps:` line format, the "recount both inventories ... without your lists" step, and "Don't silently exclude difficult cases". But the only assertion on the claim gate is the prefix "Claim 100% only when both inventories have no unmapped items". A skill that said "Claim 100% only when both inventories have no unmapped items." and dropped the requirement that the independent recount agrees, or the review of every observable branch, would still pass every assertion here. The recount step would still be present, but nothing would tie it to the completeness claim. That behavior violates the independent-review clause. The other skill tests, `bundled_skills_are_five_skill_directories_each_home_to_its_topics` and `bundled_skill_descriptions_say_when_to_use_them`, are marked for other requirements. They check structure and description wording, not this gate.

Recorded the second assessment (`false`).

text: Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase. The skill MUST direct agents to read the code and tests, map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example, identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement, and report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review.

output.rationale:
`requirements.cli.bootstrap_skill` has no structural obligation that needs implementation evidence beyond the supplied root, `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md`. That root is the bundled skill itself.

Clauses I considered:
- "Habeas MUST bundle a skill for deriving initial requirements from an existing codebase". The skill exists at `assets/skills/habeas-bootstrap-requirements/SKILL.md`, in the `assets/skills` directory that the search showed `Cargo.toml` registers as `package.metadata.symposium.skills`. The text names no mechanism, library or API for bundling. A different packaging mechanism that shipped the same skill would give the same observable result. So the mechanism is discretionary and not a structural obligation.
- "direct agents to read the code and tests". These are content directives. The skill meets them in `section[Bootstrap%20requirements]/section[Workflow]` (step 2: read the requirements, documentation, public entry points, implementation and tests).
- "map every first-party test to at least one requirement or example". The skill meets this in `section[Inventories]` (the **Tests** inventory) and `section[Tagging]` (every test must end up with a `{test}` reference, and a test no requirement states goes on the gap list).
- "identify and map every source unit implementing end-user-visible functionality or interactions to a requirement". The skill meets this in `section[Inventories]` (the **Items and behavior** inventory, including the observable surface by hand) and `section[Tagging]` (map each inventoried item to the requirement whose root reaches it; an item that fits no requirement goes on the gap list).
- "report gaps rather than claim complete coverage without an independent inventory review". The skill meets this in Workflow step 8 (a fresh subagent recounts both inventories), `section[Report]` (the template with an `Independent recount` line and a `Gaps` list), and the rule to claim 100% only when the recount agrees.

These last three clauses are obligations on how agents behave when they follow the skill's text. They are not constraints on how code is built. A reworded skill that gave the same directives would satisfy them, so no further implementation root is needed.
